title: fallback: fast-path gating + precision toggles + safe-mode for runtime kernels
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Motivation: The serving runtime exposes multiple execution paths (fast-path optimized kernels and a conservative correctness path). Recent incidents and internal benchmarks showed cases where aggressive fast-path decisions produce subtle correctness differences (quantization corner-cases, KV-cache alignment on model shims) or cause intermittent kernel failures on certain GPU/driver combos. This PR introduces an explicit fast-path gating mechanism, user-configurable precision toggles, and a runtime "safe-mode" that forces the conservative correctness path when instability is detected.

What this changes (high level):
- Add a fast-path gate in kernel selection: runtime now evaluates a small predicate (model compatibility + kernel health metrics + sequence length heuristics) before choosing the optimized kernels. If the gate fails, scheduler falls back to the conservative kernel implementation.
- Precision toggles: expose per-runtime and per-model precision hints (fp16, bf16, tf32, fp32) that are considered by kernel_selector. These toggles can be overridden by policy (customer config, Dedicated runtime config).
- Safe-mode: a lightweight runtime health monitor toggles safe-mode when it observes repeated kernel errors, correctness regressions from the QA prompt-suite, or when the driver reports kernel crashes. Safe-mode forces deterministic, higher-precision kernels and disables certain micro-optimizations (aggressive batching heuristics, fused attention variants).
- KV cache compatibility checks: ensure prefix/KV cache layout compatibility between fast-path kernels and conservative kernels during a gated fallback. Add zero-copy fallback adaptation where possible to avoid cache rebuilds.
- Continuous batching interaction: batching scheduler is now aware of gate outcomes. If fast-path is gated off in the pool, batching will use conservative batching parameters to avoid mixing kernel paths in the same batch which can cause scheduling complexity.
- Observability and rollout: new metrics (runtime.fastpath.allowed, runtime.fastpath.denied_reason, runtime.safe_mode.enabled, runtime.precision.effective) and alert rules. Rollout is feature-flag controlled and gated by a canary that monitors QA prompt-suite regressions.

Implementation notes:
- kernel_selector.rs: new predicate logic + health cache.
- precision.rs: lightweight config parsing and effective-precision computation.
- fallback.rs: safe-mode monitor, error counters, deterministic fallback code paths.
- scheduler/mod.rs: batcher checks to avoid cross-path mixing and updated autoscaling signals when safe-mode is active.
- kv_cache adapter: added compatibility shim and unit tests for prefix retention across kernel swaps.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Unit tests: new tests cover predicate outcomes, precision resolution, and KV cache adapter behavior (runtime/tests/fallback_integration.rs).
- Integration: canary harness runs QA prompt-suite to detect subtle regressions.
- Benchmarks: documented perf tradeoffs in benchmarks/fallback_bench; typical gains: 1.8-2.6x token throughput on short sequences with fast-path allowed; regressions of 0.8-0.95x on extremely long sequences (seq>=4096) for certain models due to different KV layout.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged rollout starting with internal canary (10% of traffic) for 48 hours.
- Monitor runtime.safe_mode.enabled and QA regression rate; if >0.1% regression or kernel error spike, auto-roll back to previous flag.

Related Linear/JIRA: ENG-4678, ENG-4721.

Checklist:
- [x] unit tests added
- [x] integration tests added for canary
- [x] perf benchmarks recorded
- [x] docs updated (docs/runtime/fallback.md)
- [x] observability added

Notes: This change aims to reduce incidents caused by aggressive fast-paths while preserving most of the perf benefits. The safe-mode intentionally favors correctness and will be opt-in via policy for Dedicated/private customers with strict determinism requirements.

merge_commit_message:
squash: fallback: fast-path gating + precision toggles + safe-mode

Fast-path gating predicate, precision resolution, safe-mode monitor, KV cache adapter, scheduler adjustments, tests, and docs. Can be feature-flagged for controlled rollout (ENG-4678, ENG-4721).
release_notes: Added fast-path gating and a safe-mode fallback to prioritize correctness in unstable environments. Introduced precision toggles (fp16/bf16/tf32/fp32) that can be configured per-runtime or per-model. New metrics: runtime.fastpath.allowed, runtime.fastpath.denied_reason, runtime.safe_mode.enabled, runtime.precision.effective. Rollout is feature-flagged and will begin with an internal canary.
